references.text: The Gibeonites came to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal and claimed they came from a distant land, which turned out to be a lie.
The Gibeonites repeated their lie that they came from a very distant land because of the name of the Lord.
Three days after the covenant was made, the Israelites discovered that the Gibeonites lived nearby.
Isaac confronts Jacob with words about his deceit, similar to how Joshua confronted the Gibeonites regarding their deception.
Jacob confronts Laban with the words 'Why have you deceived me?', a similar pattern of confrontation after deception.
The proverb warns against those who deceive their neighbor and say 'I was only joking', highlighting the seriousness of the Gibeonites' deception.
The command not to lie to one another, which the Gibeonites broke when they lied about where they came from.
Paul urges believers not to lie to one another, a principle that the Gibeonites violated.
